utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I understand you have some preliminary matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Just one matter, Your Honour. It's rather brief, actually. We received at approximately 10 a.m. this morning a list of documents tendered by the Office of the Prosecutor to be used in cross-examination of the witness that is on the stand, and for the record several of these documents were not available previously, were never disclosed previously including photographs that purport to show my client in uniform, which I believe ought to have been disclosed previously. I will have an objection if they try to use some of these in cross-examination, but my concern -- is that the -- it's my understanding that the practice [indiscernible] this courtroom was as has been in other cases I've been in that documents for cross-examination ought to be noticed to the opposing party when the witness takes the stand and takes the oath, and this was not done in this case on rather, massive scale, and I repeat that this witness is one that they've known about since I believe May or June of last year as this witness originally under pseudonym had been one of the initial witnesses disclosed within the alibi notification that was done at that time. So I'm concerned that we're getting late disclosure of documents intended for cross as early as this morning so that I have just now been able to print up these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, do you know the adage, what is sauce for the goose is sauce for the gander? Are you aware of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm aware of the adage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Because I believe you had -- the Prosecutor had the same complaints about the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't know about the entire time. I wasn't obviously in the case the entire time, but I do know that is out there as a rule or as a directive. I don't know the exact status of it, but I do believe any documents or photographs relating to my client have to be disclosed under either Rules 68 or 66(A).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, it's interesting that in this case as in most cases the parties have the same complaints about each other in relation to procedure and matters. I am not a slave to procedure, and you have benefitted from that attitude on my part. I believe that procedural rules must sub-serve the wider and broader and more important purpose of achieving justice, and that is what I am looking at, and I want to ensure that no party is disadvantaged and prejudiced by any late notification, and that is what will guide me in determining any objection that is raised. I don't say the rules don't have any importance. They are there, and I expect them to be followed, but ultimately I'm concerned with the wider purpose of achieving justice. Now, let us continue with the case. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just about to begin my cross-examination of Mr. Djeric, so if he could be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let Mr. Djeric be brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I'm not sure if you wish to make a statement under 15 bis before he comes in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have to say that in the absence of Judge Van Den Wyngaert, Judge David and I sit pursuant to 15 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric, I'm Dermot Groome, and I will represent the Prosecution here and ask you a few questions. Are you able to hear me through your headset?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd like to begin -- you told us yesterday that you were a member of the Army of Republika Srpska, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you were assigned to the Rogatica Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the Rogatica Brigade is a military battalion that's part of the Army of the Republika Srpska, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, it was the Army of Yugoslavia and then the Army of Republika Srpska from April to May, and June it became VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how long was it in existence? Let me put it another way. Was it in existence throughout the course of the war, which ended in 1995?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Rogatica Brigade? Well, it existed throughout the war. Until the end of the war it existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, can you give me your sense, as someone who was involved in the heart of Bosnia engaged in this conflict, what was your sense about when the conflict began and when it ended?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beginning of April, the conflict began, and it ended with the Dayton Accords.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So that is April 1992 as the beginning and the Dayton accords in the fall of 1995 as the end, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And during that entire time, were there armed confrontations between members of the VRS such as yourself and members of the Bosnian Federation Army?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how would you describe the geographic area that this combat -- these combat activities took place in?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How would you -- is it fair to say that over the majority of Bosnia there was active combat operations during this time period including Visegrad, Rogatica, Srebrenica, all of these areas in Eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Conflicts were very frequent towards Zepa, Gorazde, Visegrad, Rogatica. Very often, not constantly day in and day out, but every couple of days there were skirmishes, conflicts all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. I'd now like to ask you about how you came to know Mr. Milan Lukic. Now, from your testimony yesterday, I took from it that you met him somewhere around January 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the beginning of January, 3rd or 4th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to that, had you had any contact with Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I believe you told us that you were introduced to Milan Lukic through one of his relatives. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Bozo Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you shared a drink at a hotel bar that lasted approximately 45 minutes; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And after that time, you did not see him again until you met him in Kopito on the 14th of June, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see him in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, after your encounter with him in June of 1992, how many times have you met him after that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a time I did not see him because I had some problems with my eye. I underwent surgery, so I did not see him for a long time, but in 1996 I saw him on several occasions. He had a cafe there, and we would come for drinks and then talk, and after that I saw him on the eve of St. Nicholas Day, 18th of December. I went there with a friend of mine to have a drink, and after that I did not see him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that was what year?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1996. 18th of December, 1996. This was the last time I saw him. The 19th December is St. Nicholas Day, and Miso Bojovic [phoen], my best man, celebrates that feast.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And between the time of 1996 and the time you saw him here yesterday, had you been in contact with him, or did you see him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the record records you as saying he had a cafe there. Did you mean that Milan Lukic had a cafe?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Lukic had a cafe. It is a shopping mall at the -- Visegrad, and he had a cafe there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you please physically describe Milan Lukic as you remember him from 1992 or even 1996? How tall would you say he was as you recall him from the days before you saw him here?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember him well. He's slightly taller than I am. I'm 185, 186 centimetres. He was a lot thinner than today, and I used to be a lot thinner than I am today. He wasn't skinny. He was elegantly built.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you be able to approximate his weight?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to 90 kilos. Not more, I'm certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, there seemed to be a little bit of difficulty in translating --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, did you mean his weight at that time or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. At that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The 90 kilos, was that your assessment of his weight back when you knew him in the 1990s?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He's tall. He's close to 190 centimetres tall. I know that he's a bit taller than I am. Then 85 to 90 kilos, which would mean that he wasn't overweight.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, Mr. Ivetic actually pointed Milan Lukic out to you. He told you where he was in the courtroom, and he actually turned and pointed in the direction of Milan Lukic. Did you need him to do that in order to recognise Milan Lukic here yesterday?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no need for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you recognise Milan Lukic when you came into the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did it take you to recognise Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, some might say that it's implausible for you to be able to recognise him to quickly after such a long period of time. Is there any doubt in your mind that the Milan Lukic you saw in the courtroom is the same person that you knew from the 1990s?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One million per cent. He's gained some weight, the same as I have. I'm 1 million per cent that's Milan Lukic. I'm sure that that's Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you described remembering -- and you described in rather precise detail the uniform he was wearing when you saw him on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that ERN 0644-6670, 0644-6670, it's just a single document, could I ask that be called up for the witness to view.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, there's a TV screen to your right. I'm going to ask that you be shown a photograph on that screen. Could I ask that we focus on the bottom photograph, maybe even focus on Milan Lukic if that assists the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is one of the documents that I had mentioned earlier. This is a document that was just disclosed to us this morning at 10.00. I would object to this document without knowing the provenance of the document, the date it was taken, whom it was taken by or at least the time period it was taken in because, of course, it's quite relevant material in terms of establishing this document and whether it can be used for the purpose of the question. Now, granted there hasn't been a question yet asserted, so I have reserved the right to object to specific questions, but as far as the use of the document is concerned, I do have an objection based upon those grounds. This was never previously disclosed to us, even though now we have Mr. Groome saying it shows Mr. Milan Lukic. I believe then it ought to have been disclosed previously.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for His Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, two points. First, an explanation as for the late disclosure, and secondly, the provenance of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The document is from the court file from the case -- the court file from Serbia of the case against Milan Lukic and other people for the incident that occurred at Severin. We asked for this court file. It a very, very large file. We've been going through it as we get it translated, and we have made disclosures from this file with respect to documents that we determined were Rule 68 or contained 66(A)(ii) material. On the 31st of January, we sent a letter to Defence counsel letting him know that we had this very large file and offering them the same opportunity to view the file as us, still telling them that we realised it was our obligation to get it translated and to ferret out any Rule 68 material but offering them the opportunity to come and view that file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The 31st of January?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Of 2008 is when we sent a letter to Defence counsel, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 2009, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I'm misspeaking. 31st of December, 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: 31st of December, 2008?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So sir, can I ask you to take a look at this photograph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. I have to consider whether you have given us sufficient explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, the Chamber considers that you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, this is a black and white photograph, but can I ask you as best you're able, can you look at the uniform -- well, first of all, do you recognise Milan Lukic in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to take the pen in front of you and circle his face.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, again, this photograph is a black and white photograph, so we don't have the benefit of the colour, but you described his uniform as being a combat fatigue; I think you said camouflage yesterday. Is it similar to the uniform that we see him dressed in in this picture?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you greater detail. He had a vest. It was a chilly night, lined with something that looked like fur. It was a variegated multi-coloured vest.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The variegated, multi-coloured uniform, is that what is commonly called a camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And looking at his facial features there and his hair, is that how you remember him from the period 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw him, his hair was slightly shorter than in this picture, and he might have been a bit skinnier. Maybe this picture does not do him credit, but I do believe that he was slimmer than in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from those differences, it does appear to be the Milan Lukic as you remember him in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you be shown another photograph. It's 0644-6664. Again, it's from the same court file. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P216, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, Your Honour, I must object and stress that the e-mail disclosing this batch does not have these photographs, and these photographs obviously do not need to be translated. So they withheld these photographs which on first blush, they should have been able to immediately recognise this is material they ought to have disclosed to the Defence, so they've not disclosed it until this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, did I understand you earlier to say that this was sent on the 31st of December, 2008, to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, what we disclosed on the 31st was documents that after reviewing -- we're still in the process of reviewing this file. It's an enormous file. It's an entire trial that took place in Belgrade several years ago, and I point out, You Honour, that the file -- Defence counsel had the same access to the file, and I would hope that someone representing a client would seek out their earlier court cases. We sought out the court case. We received it. We're in the process of going through it, translating it, looking for Rule 68 material. On the 31st of December, we disclosed what we had already identified as Rule 68 material, and we said to -- in the letter -- and I'm paraphrasing because I don't have the letter in front of me. We said we have this large volume of material which we are reviewing present. You are invited to come, look at this file. There may be material. We described what the file was, and we offered them a copy of the file or an opportunity to come and view it, and that was done on the 31st of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So your answer to the objection is that you disclosed the file on the 31st of December, it's a large file, and included in that file is the photograph in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So your point is that Mr. Ivetic and the Defence, if they had examined the file, would have seen the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't have custody of the file. It's still with the Prosecution, Your Honour. They sent that e-mail knowing that I'm traveling because I'd sent an e-mail saying I'm traveling. And I gave the opportunity to meet with the originals that I had in my possession that they needed to review. So when I'm in the region traveling trying to get witnesses to come here and they say, Oh, we have this huge amount of documents that we have in our possession that we're not going to give to you, is that a disclosure under the rules that is sufficient when they have materials of this nature?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, you're traveling, but you're not alone. You have others working with you. It's not personal to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I was the only person in The Hague, Your Honours. That's the -- that's the way it is, especially with the way the cases are funded. I don't know if Your Honour's familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just point out also, I didn't have my rules handy. I didn't want to misspeak. What the provision that deals with photographs is 66 (B): "The Prosecutor shall on request permit the Defence to inspect any books, document, photographs, and tangible objects in the Prosecutor's custody or control." We advised him on the 31st about the existence of this file. The judgement on this case is down on their exhibit list as 65 ter number 63, so either they've gotten this file independently or they've looked through the copy that we've given them and have added it to their 65 ter list but seems to be a clear indication that Milan Lukic Defence is aware of this file just as we are aware of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, my inclination would be to say that it has been disclosed to you, but are you able to tell me in what specific way you have been prejudiced?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At present, no, because they have not asked questions about this particular exhibit or document. It's not an exhibit yet, but this particular document, and I don't know about any others that are in there, but again with the time period that we have ongoing in the case, how we're supposed to review a voluminous file that's only in their custody, I don't know how to do it. I applied to the Court for instructions as to how we're supposed to proceed in such a manner, but it just seems like we're constantly running up against this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you are not alone in the case. There is Mr. Alarid. I haven't seen him, but I presume Mr. Alarid is still lead counsel in the case. You have assistants. You have a case manager.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Under the trial strategy, we're only allowed one paid assistant, Your Honour, and during the break, with the way the OLAD works, we are not supposed to be working in The Hague. They actually do not pay for DSA during the break session, and the trial strategy that they have does not foresee work during the break according to the communications that I've received. I had to -- I usually have to specifically operate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Tell me specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you saying that in re-examination, because you have a right to re-examine, you would not be able to ask questions of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I haven't said that yet because I don't know what the questions are yet. I might not be embarrassed by the questions. I don't know. It's premature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us proceed. If we get to that point, then you can inform me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to take a look at another photograph. 0644-6664. It is another photograph from the same file from the court in Belgrade of Milan Lukic. Can you look at this uniform and tell us, is this similar to the uniform that he was wearing at that time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell the colour of this uniform. He didn't wear any head-gear. He did not have any other insignia except for milicija or police. This one was not for sure. It was multi-coloured but not this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And how about the weapon that he's holding there? Is that the weapon -- do you recognise the weapon?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is an automatic rifle, short, not with a wooden but a shorter version of an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall the weapon he had when you saw him in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly at that time, automatic rifles had long wooden butts. Some had machine guns 84. Some had semi-automatic rifles. There were different types of weapons in circulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to take the pen and circle the area where you remember seeing this emblem that indicated he was with the police.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you see any emblem on the uniform in that location now?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've circled a portion of his uniform on the left shoulder. Is that the arm that the emblem was on?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was on the left arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P217, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, I was a bit confused with your testimony about the different locations yesterday, so I'm going to ask that you be shown a map, and I'm going to ask you to mark the map, and I'm going to ask that the map, which is 65 ter number 176, it's going to be a map of the area of Visegrad to Rogatica. Before you do mark it, before you do mark it, I would ask you just to allow me to give you my instructions so that it's clear what the marks mean, that it agrees with the record. Now, it's probably impossible for you to see now. We'll enlarge it as much as possible. I believe Rogatica is to the left and Visegrad is to the right. Please let me know if you'd like us to enlarge it more to make it easier for you to see.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. They've enlarged the section. Of course when we enlarge the map, there's less of it that we can see, so right now the left-hand side of the map has been enlarged. Can you see the words "Rogatica" or the word "Rogatica"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And could I ask the court usher just to move it slowly, just like that, until we see Visegrad on the right side of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And now we can see the river Drina, and we can see the word "Visegrad." Do you see that now, sir.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask that we zoom out again so we can see both Rogatica and Visegrad. Now, sir, in your testimony you were talking about this road that you said was the main road, and you described it as being an important road. Can you see that road on this map?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not now. I can't see it here. The main and only communication was through Visegrad through Borike to Rogatica. Visegrad through Borike to Rogatica. This is the road along the Drina River which was not passable at the time through Medjedja. It was not passable for us, Serb army. Visegrad, Borike, Rogatica. That was the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask if the usher could enlarge the left half of the map. Maybe we can do it in two parts to see if that assists the witness. Do you see coming out of Rogatica there's a thick line, and it goes all the way to Visegrad? Passes through Kopito, through Borike, Sjemec.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sjemec. The name that you pronounced was Sjemec.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you see that road on the map in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see the line, but I'd like to see it enlarged. I just see a line, nothing more than that. I can't see Borike on the map. I would like to have it enlarged. The most important road here is the Visegrad-Borike road through Sjemec. I'd like that section to be enlarged if possible, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can that be done?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it assist you in seeing a hard copy of the map?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me take a look, yes. Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before this is shown to the witness, this is my copy. It has two words, Kladanj and Rujiste, up in the right-hand corner. I don't believe it's going to be considered leading any way, but could I ask that Mr. Ivetic just look at the map before it is shown to the witness to see if he has any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, we're going to give you a hard copy of the map that we were trying to work with in electronic form. Can you get your bearings on that map now?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it be easier for you to work and mark that map than the electronic one?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to ask you to make some marks for us about the locations you've described in your testimony. Would it be easier if I asked you to do it on the hard copy rather than on the television screen?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's really all the same, if we could only just zoom in on this portion and then I could see the individual villages and places better, but I can use both equally well. I can use the one or the other. It's just a matter of zooming in on the specific portion. Perhaps if we could just get this portion blown up, and then I'd still be perfectly able to follow everything on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think it may actually make sense because I'm going to ask you to make markings all over the map to work on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So if I could ask the usher to maybe turn on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And then I'm going to ask you to make some marks on that map. And again, sir, if you'd wait until I give you an instruction about what I'd like to you mark, I think it'll -- the end product will be more understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, could I ask that the witness be given a fine-lined pen because the villages are small.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, while we're getting you a pen, could I ask you to study the map and ask you, would you be able to indicate the road that you've spoken about yesterday in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you be given the blue pen, and could I ask you to simply trace the road between Visegrad and Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see Borike in this map. Krsmanovici, Brankovici, I see all of those, but I can't see what it says here, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you see Rogatica on that map?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm telling you about the other road through Borike. That's where I started out from. We went from Rogatica to Borike, and after Borike there was the HQ, and then from Borike through Sjemec, we went on to Kopito, Gornja Lijeske; Gornja Lijeske on to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us where the road was blocked? Again, I'd ask you not to let the tip of the pen touch the map until you have an instruction from me.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the road. This is Borike and this is the road through Stavanj. This is Stavanj. I can't see Stavanj. Here it is. That's the road. So -- just a minute, please. Around Brdo, that's it. All right. These bends here, a series of bends, is where Kopito is. Gornja Lijeske, Donja Lijeske, and then Kopito, and then there it is. If that's what it says what I'm pointing at. Is this Sjemec there, what I'm pointing at? I can't see it properly. It's reads something like that, but I don't know. Yeah, there's the road, that's the road over there, and yes -- and then over there, there is a series of bends here, and then the first series of bends and then Gornja Rijeka, and that's where Vlatko Tripkovic got killed at, Gornja Rijeka. And over here, to somewhere around here, over here, around here. Where I was ambushed, that's here, the last series of bends before Kopito, that's where.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay, sir, to do this in an orderly fashion, can I ask you to draw the road as best you can. If you have to approximate it, then do so, but draw the road as best you're able that you were referring to yesterday in your testimony. Are you able to do that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Just a minute, please. Take it easy. I'm getting to it. That's the cross-roads, so right here, this is Borike, the cross-road after Rogatica and after Sjemenic [phoen], this cross-road right here, that's it. There you go. Krsmanovic, Brankovic -- just a minute. Please let me see. This way?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is the pen working? I don't see any mark.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's weak. It's not working properly. Borike -- all right. The cross-road after Rogatica, this one, and this one to Sjemenic on to Visegrad, so this way, and then around here. There you have it. I marked the one over here, so this is the road that I marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think you were using that defective pen for the rest of the journey. Can I ask you just to retrace that with that marker now, all the way to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think we can see that now. Can I ask you just to draw a line through "Kladanj" and "Rujiste" at the top of the map that's not markings that you made, so if you just draw a line through those two words. See at the very top right-hand corner of the map, it has two words, hand-written, "Kladanj" and "Rujiste"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So can you just draw a line through them since they are not your marks?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can I ask you to write your name at the top of the map so we'll know that it's you who made these marks on the map.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, can I ask you, with a simple "X," can you show us where along that road you tell us it was blocked on the 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to -- well, if he's referring to the witness's testimony, he should give a transcript page, I think, as to which particular reference he's referring to so we can have the full context of the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it in dispute that he said the road was blocked? I thought that was the entire nature of the alibi.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But if you're citing to him what his testimony is, which part of the -- of his testimony? Perhaps I didn't catch the whole question. I thought you were asking about -- he'd drawn something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Perhaps I have it wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, was the road blocked on the 14th of June? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 14th of June? Yes, 14th of June it was blocked. The blockade was lifted no sooner than the 15th. The 15th, the morning of the 15th, an operation was launched to lift the blockade. I drew only to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you just to draw an X across the spot on the road where you say he was blocked? I see you've drawn one line of the X. Can you just simply draw the remainder of the X to show us where the road was blocked. Again, there seems to be a problem with the pen.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I marked it. Right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... the witness had drawn previously a single line to which Mr. Groome referred. What was that meant to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you understand what Judge Robinson is asking you, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This first line that I drew right here, the first one is the place where found the soldiers and the police who were together, and that's where I conveyed to news to them, and the other place that I indicated was the place where Vlatko Tripkovic was killed, the mark lower down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, it'll get terribly confusing if you make marks aside from my instruction. What I'm interested in you marking is where the road was blocked. Was that the same place where Tripkovic was killed? Without making any mark, was the road blocked where Tripkovic was killed, or was that a different location?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We couldn't even get to that location, but the location that I've marked, the first one, that's where the operation took place, and that man Djeric had been killed three days previously, and they wanted to evacuate the dead. It was blocked there, and one could proceed no further. One couldn't proceed any further than that. I explained about the first place at Kopito, and then you couldn't get further down that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So as I understand it, and please correct me if I'm wrong, the first line that you made, which is just a single line across the road, is where the road was blocked. It was impossible for anyone to get across that area. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the blockade. It wasn't that it was blocked. One just couldn't proceed in that direction because some people had been killed there, and they were evacuating from those houses. The soldiers were there to evacuate those people who were in those houses who were dead, and they couldn't manage for one, two, three days before that, and that's where the soldiers were, and that's where this portion between these two portions was. It was quite inaccessible. You have bends in the road there, thick woods, that sort of thing, and all the problems that were occurring in that area between the line that I drew now. The first line that I drew now and the second line that I drew now, that's the area that was totally unsecured, and as soon as there is an incident, one just can't get through. I mean, I'm not sure you understand because there's a difference, you know, the distance between the two roads being about 10 kilometers or thereabout.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So correct me if I'm wrong. So it's really the space between the two marks you made across the road, that was the portion if of the road that it was impossible to go past. Is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever there's an incident, one can't get through. This is entirely unsecured, from the Rogatica road from the Visegrad road, it was never secured, that part of the road. It was only when we secured it when it wasn't blocked then. And the Rogatica and the Visegrad Brigade, and they all covered those ten kilometers, and then it was safe. But other than that, whenever there's an incident, it's always blocked. One can't get through before it's cleared.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, again with the blue pen, can I ask you to circle the entire portion of the road that you say was insecure and people could not get through. I have a blue pen if it assists.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want you to make a few other marks. Rogatica we can see clearly on the map. Visegrad we can see clearly on the map. Can I ask you to put the letter "B" as to where Borike is located.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to put a "K" to indicate where Kopito is located.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to put an "S" where Sjemec - and can you please excuse my pronunciation - is located.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Sjemec field. That's what it's called. Sjemec is a relative concept. It's actually a mountain. So this is the section that you probably mean. That's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've made a circle on a section of the road. Can I ask you to put an "S" inside that section so we know that that's the Sjemec part of the road.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, is it possible to show Kovanj on the map? Am I correct in saying that Kovanj is west of Rogatica, and it's not on this map?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kovanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. Again, excuse my pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kovanj is off the map. One needs to go from Rogatica to Sokolac. It's the first village one comes across down that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And Sokolac is off that map, as well, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you circle Sokolac for us on the map?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not here. It's off the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How about Jabuka, J-a-b-u-k-a? Is that also off the map?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it. It's in the direction of Gorazde heading out from Rogatica. But you take a different road across the mountain and not along the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And finally the last location I just want to confirm with you is not on that map, and that's Zakomo, Z-a-k-o-m-o.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see Zakomo either. It's not on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I admit that map. Sorry, I would tender that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P218, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, now, I'm going to be showing you a few military reports, and that's why I was asking you some of these different names. Am I correct in saying that if someone were to say there was a problem on the Rogatica-Borike segment of the road, they're referring to the portion of the road between Rogatica and Borike. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you were working as a soldier in this area, if there was a problem between -- on the road between Rogatica and Borike, how would you communicate that? What phrase would you use to communicate that that's where the problem was?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would tell them there's a problem somewhere. I'm not really sure what you're driving at. Can you try to elaborate? I didn't understand the nature of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm being unclear. If we had a military report that said there was combat on the Kopito-Visegrad segment of the road, would the military report say, combat on the Kopito-Visegrad segment? Is that how it would be identified?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they said Kopito, then they would know where it was. Donja Rijeka, Kopito, that's the road from Borike to Visegrad. That's clear enough. One knows where Kopito is. Everybody knows that, clear enough. They would say a problem at Kopito, and then everybody would be perfectly up to date.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What would they say if it was between -- if it was half-way between Kopito and Visegrad? How would they identify that part of the road?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above Gornja Lijeske, above Gornja Lijeske. That would have been the reference point. Between Visegrad and Kopito, about mid-way in between, just further up from Gornja Lijeske would be the mid-point between the two. I'm talking about Kopito on the one hand and Visegrad on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What's the approximate distance between Kopito and Visegrad, the town of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 15 kilometers, 16 perhaps. I didn't exactly measure it, but I think that should be in the ball park.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And given the terrain and the hair-pin turns, how long should it take someone to drive from Kopito to Visegrad if there was no blockage in the road and no traffic, if you could just drive from Kopito to Visegrad? How long would that take?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a slow journey, very slow. Just before the Kopito peak, you have a series of bends, and then past Gornja Lijeske, again, another series of bends. Between Gornja Lijeske and Kopito, 90 per cent of that section is hair-pin bends, very sharp bends, difficult to drive. If you drive there, you're in first gear up to second gear, perhaps. Third gear, hardly use at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it take more than a half an hour?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that much is certain. If you drive carefully and safely, over half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it take more than an hour?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might. It might, if there are no problems, if the car is solid and in good working order.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just to correct the transcript. I believe -- and the question at line -- the answer at line 16, I believe the witness had said it could be done in half an hour, it could if there are no problems. It says, "it might." I don't know how we want to deal with that. Do we need to a request to have the audio listened to, Your Honour? It seems like the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I can clarify with just an additional question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic is not sure that the transcript has recorded you accurately. Is it your evidence that the trip between Kopito and Visegrad could be done in a half an hour, that it is possible to do it in a half an hour?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. In an hour. In an hour. He said at line 16, it's when he's talking about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So is it your evidence -- sir, the easiest thing is if you can just tell us, how many minutes would it take to get from Kopito to Visegrad? Then it'll be clear. If you know its approximation.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said is this: If one drives fast, if one takes risks, maybe half an hour, but if you drive safely, regularly, you couldn't do it in under an hour, so let's try to calculate a mean, about 45 minutes. So I'd put it somewhere between half an hour and one hour, depending on who's doing the driving, depending on what sort of a vehicle is involved, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That's very helpful. Now, I took from your testimony yesterday that this particular road that you've now marked on the map is a very important road logistically -- or was a very important road logistically in 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only road that we from the Rogatica Brigade had on our way to Serbia or to Visegrad, that was the only road that we could use. Another thing that was important was that the Muslims also needed this road. This was a corridor for them. It's not a surfaced road, but it's a road they used through the woods from Zepa to Gorazde. It was at Kopito of all places, between Gornja Lijeske and Kopito. That's where they made their crossings. Everything that they carried across from Zepa to Gorazde, they used that road, and we from Zepa to Rogatica also used the same road in order to get stuff to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So am I correct in saying that it was a vital artery for military supplies and food supplies for the Rogatica Brigade, and if you can answer it simply yes or no, perhaps we can move a little bit quicker.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And am I right in saying that any blockage on this road would have significance for military purposes?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not -- it doesn't matter who was actually in control of that section of the road, but that's what I'm telling you about. It's a 10-kilometer stretch. It would have been difficult. Nobody had enough man-power to keep it under control, to keep it covered all the time. They would use 100- and 200-metre stretches just to cover it, and then they would take cover whenever possible and then when they wanted the army from the other sides to withdraw, because the Rogatica municipality territory is quite large. You have the part towards Borike, the part towards Zepa. And in order to secure that part of the road, you would need all the of the soldiers, the whole brigade to got here and secure the area, so you could never be entirely covered, you know, fully covered. The whole area, it was -- what should I call it, a bit risky, the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about what it took to safe-guard the road. All I'm asking you is, if it's impossible to use that road for the Army of Republika Srpska, that has military significance, does it not? It affects military operations, it affects military resupply? Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. No supplies could possibly come through, food or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, yesterday -- I want to go back now to your military service. Yesterday you stated that you were stationed in Borike. Is that where you were first stationed when you joined the unit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you always under the command of a person by the name of Rajko Kusic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rajko Kusic, he was the brigade commander. Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was your title or rank under Rajko Kusic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got my rank towards the end of my service, war-time service. I was the company commander, but that's how it was for a while. The Borike company, specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, Mr. Ivetic spent 45 minutes. You have so far used 52, and I'll give you another 8 or 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask for some leniency just with all the difficulties we had with the map, I think it was absolutely essential for the Chamber to have the map, but I do have a number of very important documents that I want to try and work with the witness. I'm not sure that I can do it in 8 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How much time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll see how we get along, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, as part of your duties as company commander, would you make reports to Rajko Kusic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We just had working meetings, briefings, and tasks were handed out. In concrete terms, I was tasked with defending Borike from the direction of Zepa. We had our lines there, and this was my task, to defend this line and those trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My time is quite limited, so if possible I'd ask you to just answer the questions as shortly or as briefly as you're able. I want to show you a report. You described an incident on the 27th of June yesterday. I want to ask that you be shown 0642-9694, and again, on the screen in front of you there's going to be a report that we received from the Republika Srpska when we asked for the records of your unit. It'll take a few seconds to get it up, but what I want you to look at is, I believe this report refers to the incident that you were telling us about yesterday on the 27th, and I want you to read the report and confirm, is this a report of the incident you testified to yesterday?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If in could be enlarged a bit for me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's the first paragraph of that report that I think refers to -- are you able to read it now?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please review it, and when you've done that, let us know if that's an accurate report of what happened on the 27th.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The van was not protected, and the Yugo car was not there. We had two vehicles. One was Lada, a white Lada, and another was a police Volkswagen Golf.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask that you look at the bottom of the document where it's signed by Kusic or for Kusic. Do you recognise the seal and your superior's name?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could track back to the top of the page. There was mention of a car hitting an anti-tank mine. Maybe there was another problem. If you could enlarge that section for me to read the whole paragraph. I managed to read only one or two rows. If I am allowed to read the whole paragraph, please. The top portion refers to that, yes. Can we scroll back to the signature for me to take a look at it? This signature is somebody else's. Could be Milovan Lelik in my opinion. He was deputy commander. I do believe that this is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would it be common for the deputy commander to sign for the commander on reports, on daily reports of activities in the area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the commander was absent, I presume, yes, that he would.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recognise the first portion as being a description of the event that you described yesterday, although it seems that there's some differences with respect to the makes of the cars.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is most probably a report of the Rogatica Brigades descripting one killed soldier. On that occasion, one was severely wounded, later died, and one was killed outright. The Lada vehicle carried men of the Visegrad Brigade and most probably the Visegrad Brigades prepared a report on their killing. In the Rogatica Brigade, we have a report of one killed and several severely or lightly wounded. In my vehicle, one was killed, and one was severely wounded, and that was a car belonging to Rogatica Brigade. The Lada Niva car was -- belonged to Visegrad Brigade. Goran Zecevic was killed and another soldier was wounded. This is most probably referring to the Rogatica Brigade's report. If we were to take a look at the Visegrad Brigade report of the same date, then they most probably would have reported one killed and one severely wounded in that car that belonged to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. But you do recognise the signature of the deputy commander at the bottom of the report from the 27th of June?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do believe that I can make out the word "for" in front of the word "commander," so it's on behalf of the commander somebody else signed this document. We could enlarge and take a look at it to corroborate. When it says "for the commander," this means that somebody who is authorised to do so did it on behalf of the commander, and it states here "for the commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And when you did -- when we did have it enlarged, and you looked at the signature, you said that you recognised it as the deputy commander, a person by the name of Lelik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lelik. It resembles his signature. I cannot guarantee you 100 per cent, but it is a similar signature to his, but I cannot guarantee it 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, given that, I simply ask that it be marked for identification at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P219 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, the next document that I'm going to ask you to look at is a report issued by Commander Kusic on the 13th of June, 1992, and it is 0642-9681 to 9682. While that's being called up, let me just identify it for the record. It's a regular operations report for the Army of Serbian republic of BH, SRK, Rogatica Brigade, reference number 1-98/92, Borike, dated the 13th of June, 1992, and sent to the command of the SRK. Now, directing your attention to page 2 in the B/C/S version, the document again indicates it's from Commander Kusic. Do you recognise the hand-writing of the person who signed for Kusic in this case?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was signed on behalf of the commander. This is not Rajko Kusic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you recognise Kusic's hand-writing?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, going to the first paragraph, it states -- I'll ask if that can be shown to the witness. "There were no major enemy activity this is our municipality, That is to say, in our brigade's zone of responsibility, in the Kopito Sector (Visegrad municipality), an enemy sabotage-terrorist group, which Was probably 10 to 15 men strong, attacked houses in the village and Torched a barn and a house. One member of our forces in Visegrad was Killed." And then directing your attention to ten lines from the bottom of The page, the report states: "A part of the company from Rogatica controls and secures the Rogatica-Gorazde access. A part of the units from Borike controls and Secures the Sjemec-Borike-Rogatica access, and that one squad is engaged in laying mines in the Percin sector and the general sector of Sjemec. Does the information in that report agree with your recollection of what was happening in your zone of responsibility on the 13th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We up until that time was securing the Sjemecko Polje area, We received attacks. That our responsibility to provide security up to Sjemec, that section, and there was a ramp by the road in the Sjemecko Polje, in the direction of Visegrad. We were responsible, the Rogatica Brigade, I mean, that area until Sjemec Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'd ask that this time this document be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P220 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, there's just two more of these documents I want to show you. I want to show you the report that was generated on the 14th by Commander Kusic. That is ERN 0642-9683. Again, I'll identify it for the record. It's a regular operations report from the Army of Republika Srpska, Rogatica Brigade, reference number 1-101/92, Borike, dated the 14th of June, 1992, and sent to the Command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. Now, directing your attention to page 2 in the B/C/S version, the document indicates it is from Commander Kusic again, and again, I believe we have a situation where it's signed for Kusic by one of his subordinates, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recognise the stamp or the seal as the one that was in use during this period?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This seal was used, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to direct your attention to the first paragraph, and it states: The enemy operated in several places by infiltrating sabotage and terrorist groups. Enemy activities continue being more pronounced in the area of Visegrad municipality in Kopito, Gornja Lijeske, Kocarin. Three soldiers from Visegrad were killed in yesterday's attacks by enemy sabotage groups. Enemy actions in the town of Rogatica are increasing. Fire was opened at the column of members of the Serbian Army going from Gorazde toward Sokolac." When it refers to three soldiers from Visegrad, is that the incident that you were testifying to yesterday when you talked about Tripkovic being killed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. It does correspond to the location between Kopito And Gornja Lijeske.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this be marked for Identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, and we have to take the break now. Before We take the break, let me just deal with two matters.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. This would be Exhibit P221 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yesterday, I said I would give a ruling in relation to MLD15. MLD15 is not to be recalled before Monday the 2nd of February. And in relation to the expert witnesses, the Defence is to disclose the full statements and/or reports of the six experts no later than Monday, the 26th of January, and the Prosecution is to respond by Friday the 13th of February. We are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One clarification, Your Honour, as to MLD15, I Presume that that's going to be VWS recalling him as the Defence, he's not supposed to have contact in that regard. Is that what I can report to VWS?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. VWS will be informed. We're adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, just one more document I want you to take a look at. It's ERN 0642-9685, and again, this is a report of your Commander Kusic giving A report of the events of the 15th of June, 1992. While it being called up, the title of the report is regular Report from the Army of Republika Srpska, SRK, Rogatica Brigade, Reference number 01-102/92, Borike, dated 15 June 1992, and sent to the Command of the SRK. Again, if we could go to the bottom of the signature -- the Signature line, and again, do you recognise the seal of your unit, and do You recognise the hand-writing of the person who signed this report?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not that clearly visible, I mean, the seal, but I can see That it was the Brigade seal, and it's also signed by the deputy commander of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to go to the first paragraph of this report And just read one line from it. It says: "There was no signature enemy activity in the brigade's zone of Responsibility." And then the rest of the report summarises different training activities that are ongoing and gives an account of the military stores, ammunitions that were in possession of the unit. Do you recall around This period of time that there were training activities for the unit? I Think the report mentions some trainers coming from the Republic of Serbia to do training. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what was going on at Rogatica, but at Borike, no. Rogatica Brigade held 50 kilometers of territory in diameter, but at Borike, at the time there were no instructors on the 15th, 16th of June, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'd ask that this be Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P222 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, can you just give us some idea, when reports are issued, how Long after an event are they generated? It seems that some of these Reports are referring to events that happened on the same day, some the day before. How long did it usually take for reports to be generated?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not generate any, so I don't know. I did not prepare any reports. We were an army -- an emerging army, army being built. Our mobilization rate was 105, so all men, why 105 per cent? Because people who would not otherwise be mobilised were rounded up, all the men, 60, 70 years of age, but all of them were the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, there's another witness that's due to testify after you. I'd ask if you could just answer my questions, yes or no, or the briefest explanation possible, Mr. Ivetic will have an opportunity to ask you some additional questions after I do. We now have three reports from your Commander Kusic, the 13th, the 14th, and the 15th. None of those reports mentioned a blocked road, do they?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if somebody is killed and the road is impossible, that means it is blocked. As I've mentioned, on the 27th of June the road was blockaded by the felled tree trunks, but in those events, the road was not blockaded. In this 10-kilometer stretch of road when somebody is killed, it is presumed that the road is blocked. Nobody wants to travel along it before it's mopped up and cleared. Depending on where the military was at a certain point, if the military is to go to Sjemec, this was done by the Gorazde Brigade, and up to Sjemec was held by the Visegrad Brigade, and when there is a killing, then the road is shut down and blocked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, there's no mention in any of the reports on the 13th, 14th, or 15th that communications have been interrupted, is there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you took the reports of the Visegrad Brigade, maybe they would be mentioned. In Rogatica, there was no such things. The Rogatica Brigade personnel did not have communication with Visegrad. There was no way they could have communicated through radio because in Commander Tripkovic's vehicle, the radio was destroyed, and we were tasked to inform the people at Kopito to tell them what had happened through the Rogatica Brigade, but those people belonged to the Visegrad Brigade who were at Kopito, Territorial Defence, military, and police, they had no communication with Visegrad, and so they phoned Rogatica Brigade and instructed somebody from Rogatica Brigade to go over there, contact them, and tell them what was to be done later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday you testified to when you arrived in Kopito seeing a group of 40 to 50 men involved in the operation, and then you testified, and I'm going to quote from your statement where you say it a bit more succinctly. In paragraph 2 of your statement, you say: "As earlier agreed, the campaign to secure Kopito-Visegrad road started on June 15th, 1992, around 10 a.m. As the campaign was getting underway towards Visegrad, I returned to Rogatica and informed the command of Rogatica that I have fulfilled my missions." Sir, in the reports that we have before us, the 13th, 14th, and 15th, there's no mention at all of the campaign that you've testified about, is there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that that was in the Visegrad Brigade. The one we saw was the Rogatica Brigade report. Rogatica Brigade personnel did not take part in that actio, and this is why it's not being reported. Rogatica -- Rogatica Brigade's area of responsibility ended at Sjemec. Beyond that was the zone of responsibility of Visegrad, and it wasn't in our brigade's repose because we did not do anything from Sjemec to Kopito. It was the other brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Tripkovic was killed in the zone of responsibility of the Visegrad Brigade, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yet we see that reported, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it was indicated that he was from Visegrad Brigade. Well, it is alarming when a commander is killed. In the previous report, it was mentioned that in the Visegrad Brigade's zone of responsibility three members were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that the witness's prior statement be tendered -- or I tender it. It's Y018-2196.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P223, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I have just a few more questions for you. The Defence of Milan Lukic asked for safe conduct for you to come and testify, and in their submission on this, they state, and I quote: "The witness has expressed serious concerns ..." And that's why they requested safe conduct. The serious concerns you had were related to activities that -- activities that your brigade engaged in might cause you to be arrested. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was discontinued interpretation. I heard a segment in English and not in my language. Could you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... relevant to the testimony that the witness has given, and so I would object to the relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I see that it could be relevant, Mr. Ivetic. Please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'll repeat the question now for you. The reason you asked for safe conduct to come here is that you were afraid that you might be arrested because of the activities of the unit that you were a member of. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In fact, two members of your unit, Radislav Lubinac [phoen], also known as Pano, and Dragoje Pajunovic [phoen], also known as Spiro, they've already been convicted by the State Court of Bosnia. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the other family name. I never heard of Drago Pajunovic in Rogatica. As for the former person, that was Lubinac, his family name. And what about Pano, I don't know anything of their being convicted. They weren't in my battalion. I'm telling you, I was at Borike and was in charge of that section between Zepa and Sjemec, in that area towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to show you one last report -- or this is actually an order by your commander, Rajko Kusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I ask that 0529-4778 be called up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My initial question to you is, when it comes up on the screen, is Whether or not you recognise the hand-writing as that of your commander It's a hand-written -- I'm sorry. Have I given you the wrong -- can I just check the ...

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not hand-written.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct. That's not the -- I'm sorry. It's 0107-1284. My apologies on the wrong number. This was an order that was recovered from the Kosara military barracks, in Banja Luka in June of 2006. Do you recognise the hand-writing of your superior, Rajko Kusic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is not his signature. I'm not 100 per cent Sure, but I think it is not his.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, let me read the order to you and ask you whether you have heard of this order. "No one has the right to stop military action. "There are to be no negotiations or ultimatums. "Any citizen who surrenders and brings weapons shall be Protected. Those who do not surrender and are disloyal will be persecuted and killed. "The bringing of Muslims into Serbian villages or to our military positions for negotiations are hereby forbidden. "Make it known that anyone who does not return their weapons and does not surrender will be killed." Sir, I put it to you that you asked for safe passage here because you are one of the men who carried out this order of your superior, Rajko Kusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. This was already said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The witness obviously doesn't recognise the hand-writing. There is no signature. There is no seal. They were supposed to take the Prosecutor at his word that this is a document, an official document. Who knows who wrote this. Is this what this trial is stooping to, that we're turning in hand-written sheets of paper with no seal, no title, no official letterhead, no nothing?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I haven't sought to tender it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But the question is based upon it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But the question that Mr. Ivetic is raising is whether the document is of a kind and a provenance that would warrant a question being asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I said in my question to the witness, it was recovered from the military barracks of the VRS. I will be producing the documentation regarding its provenance. The witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It seems to me that the question could be put even without the document. You could formulate the question without the aid of the document and ask the witness if he knows of any such order and whether it might have related to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll do that, Your Honour. Can I ask that it be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P 224 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm putting to you is that the reason that you requested safe passage here is because you were involved in activity which you believe makes you vulnerable to prosecution for war crimes. That's what I'm putting to you. Now I ask for your response to that. Is that why you sought safe passage?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've never seen this document, nor did I ever hear this order. I never heard this order, nor did anyone ever give me an order like this. It wasn't because of that. I told you clearly at first why this was, and then later I said that I sought no form of protection whatsoever or anything like that. I have no reason to get upset over anything at all. If I had a reason to worry, I wouldn't be here to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, are you saying that you never requested safe passage to come and testify here? Is that your evidence?
