utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't think we can take it any further, and you should be bringing your cross-examination to a close now. You have used almost twice the time allotted or used by Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just a couple more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, this past June, the 2nd of June, 2008, you were convicted of the crime of slander in the court of Obrenovac. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This hasn't taken effect yet. This was a minor thing started by a minor person, but the trial was never brought to an end. I was never made criminally responsible for anything in my life. This is a private suit brought against me by the association of Obrenovac's artisans. There was never really a final judgement on that or anything like that, and I have not been convicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let me show you the judgement of the trial court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I call up 0644-5202. This is the judgement entered on the 2nd of June, 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and again, this is a situation where, again, the judgement is not final. They're presenting a document that is still in the pending process, so just so that's on the record and that's understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, have a seat, and you can make your submissions on it. Let us see the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, while it's being called up, I'm going to read you a portion of the document, and then we can -- you can see it in its original form. It says: "On the 2nd of June, 2008, adopted and made public the following judgement: The accused Goran Djeric - for personal information, see file - is guilty because on the 27th of November, 2006, in Obrenovac, during the opening of the information business centre in front of approximately 30 people, he uttered several false claims, thus tarnishing the honour and reputation of the plaintiff who is the secretary of the Association of Obrenovac Entrepreneurs Obrenovac entrepreneurs by saying that the plaintiff 'is taking 5 percent form people he finds employment for,' that 'he was determining his own salary,' and that 'he had usurped the association,' thereby committing the crime of slander under Article 171, paragraph 1, of the Criminal Code."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There seems to be some difficulty calling up the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm advised it's not in e-court, but let us hear the answer to the question and then any submissions that Mr. Ivetic has, he may make.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, do you deny that you were convicted of this crime for uttering false statements?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I never got this sentence. Once I do, I will lodge a complaint with the district prosecutor. Perhaps I need to clarify this. I said this as a member of the executive board of that very association, that the secretary was making our working conditions impossible. You should look at that, too, but now that you have this, maybe you should have from the Obrenovac Prosecutor -- my apologies, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I just want to find out from Mr. Ivetic, the passage that was read by counsel, it said that he is guilty. Does that in the law -- and I know you're familiar with it and you're an officer of the court, so we will take your word, does that mean that he's guilty or that he's still charged? Is the charge still pending?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's my understanding that this is -- I don't have the original B/C/S in front of me, but it's my understanding that this is a transcript. It's not a judgement as was represented by Mr. Groome. I defer to Mr. Cepic who has much more practice in the region and in the jurisdiction as to what the precise legal meaning it is, but I understand it means it's still pending until it becomes a final binding judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If I may assist Your Honour, with your leave, it is not in-power document. This is just a record. It must be judgement in hard copy, which the accused and his Defence counsel received by post and also OTP, and after the decision, after they receive decision, they have eight days in this case, because this is the lowest level case, for appeal, and it is not in power. It is not decision in power, definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So you're saying it's not a final decision of the Court?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, prior to my examination, I gave the court usher the original copy to help assist with the e-court. Could I ask that the witness be shown -- oh, we have it up there now. So Mr. -- I guess I'm confused. I'm reading from the document, which says it's a judgement, which says he's guilty of a particular crime, but that's not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And if I may assist Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic. We'll hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting, but just if I may assist related to documents in the judgements for my country. Most of you are familiar that we need the stamp for almost each document in our law system, so a judgement must have the stamps, special stamps that it is in power.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: By in power, you mean that it is enforced?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Enforced. Yes, exactly. Precisely. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So even though it says -- where is this section, Mr. Groome, that says he's guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This is the fourth page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Groome, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe this is the fourth page, one of the prior pages, but here we can clearly see, Your Honour, "judgement," and in bold, "is guilty."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's from the court in Obrenovac, through it a request for assistance of the government of Serbia. What is the legal effect -- if I might ask Mr. Cepic, what is the legal effect of this document if it's -- I appreciate that he may have the right to appeal this judgement, but it seems that a trial court has entered a finding of guilty.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This is the base -- this record is the base for the filing of the judgement in the hard copy. This is not a proper form. This is just a record from the trial. After the trial is completed, the judges is in charge to file the judgement in the record. After that completion, he must file a hard copy of judgement, which will be delivered to the parties. This is just the first step in procedure. After -- this is the base for the filing in hard copy, this record of the trial. After this record -- after he files the hard copy of the judgement, he must deliver to the parties, and the parties, when they receive that hard copy, they have opportunity to file appeal in eight days. If they do not file appeal in that period of time, the judgement will be enforced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So what you're saying, then, it's only a procedural step --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- that stands between what we see here and a final guilty verdict.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Judge David.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, from the viewpoint of Article 171, paragraph 1, of -- I imagine KZ is the Criminal Penal Code, is a code of contravention?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have continental law system, and it is the criminal law procedure which allows to file the judgement just on the record, and when they filed this judgement, they invite the party, and they read the verdict in the courtroom, but the verdict is not in power. After reading in the public announcement, they must deliver that in hard copy to the parties with explanation of decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Yes, but what I am asking you is, from the legal implications of the judgement in itself as it stands now presented here, what will happen - first question - if the judgement is not sealed with the stamps?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It couldn't be in power.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: But nevertheless, it's a legal decision of the court? It's a legal decision of the court or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It is a decision, but it is quite complicated procedure, maybe, from some other points of view. It is just the first step in procedure. I'll try to make it as simple as I could. When we completed the trial procedure, the Trial Chamber rendered a decision, and they already rendered a decision in the transcript. After they render a decision, we must wait - according to law is just 8 or 15 days, but in the practices, a couple months - for the hard copy of decision, and the hard copy of decision could be just in power with those stamps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That is very clear, then, that legally has all the power subjected to the procedure of stamping or recording in getting the hard copies .

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't think we should spend any more time on this. I thank you very much, Mr. Cepic. Mr. Ivetic, in re-examination or at a later stage if you want to clarify the matter, you may do so, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions. If I could just tender that document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P 225, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, you wanted to say something because you are going to be -- yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. I do have to say this for my own sake. The Prosecutor uses this document now. The Prosecution in Obrenovac filed charges against the Secretary of the Association, and I was a witness there. When I get a copy of this sentence, it's appealable by me with the district court. They will then decide whether I'm guilty or not, and there won't be a verdict before then. It might take a year or two. Based on evidence provided by witnesses, something was - and you should find this easy to check - the Prosecutor in Obrenovac is organising proceedings against Mr. Zaric [phoen], and I'm a witness in that case. That should be easy enough to check, and it should be easy enough for you to check that at no point throughout these proceedings did I utter a lie or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's ERN 0644-6670. It's the original picture -- or the picture that was tendered of several persons in uniforms. The copy that was entered into evidence cuts off the part that I want to focus in on, so we have to return to the original as tendered by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And sir, when we get this photograph, first of all, I'd ask that we try and centre and zoom in on the man on the second photograph, on the bottom, the man sitting or squatting in the front with sunglasses, and if -- that should be fine, and if I could direct your attention, sir, to the patch or emblem on the shoulder, and I ask you if -- can you make out the lettering across the top of that patch, or does it resemble anything that you are familiar with, that lettering, that sort of half-arc with some lettering that appears to be in Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should read "police" on the left as I explained. This is probably a Serbian coat of arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djeric, for coming here to testify. On behalf of Milan Lukic and his Defence team, I thank you. I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we at this time don't have another witness in The Hague. We have one witness who was on her way and was to arrive, but the flight was cancelled due to bad weather, and the latest from VWS says she will not arrive at Amsterdam airport until 10.30 tomorrow morning, which presents us with a difficulty in that -- obviously that's -- we have court in the morning tomorrow, I believe, according to the schedule, and therefore I cannot present that witness until having proofed her, and then I would have to either present her in the afternoon, which I don't know if we have time in court then, or leave her for the next available court date, which I believe would be Monday, according to the schedule, in the afternoon, and that's -- that's Ms. Vasiljevic, the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Her flight was cancelled due to bad weather, and you say she will arrive at Schipol 10.30 tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 10.30 tomorrow morning according to VWS is when she would arrive in Schipol. It's my understanding then obviously she'd have to travel here, and they have the orientation, which at least with this batch of witness took about an hour when they received in the evening before they were released into the hotel, I guess, or whatever terminology there is. I don't know the specifics of what happens between VWS and the witnesses at that juncture since I'm not allowed access to the witnesses until after that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, clearly it's not the fault of the Defence that there is bad weather in Sarajevo. May I have a word with the legal counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber has been trying to make the best of the situation. If the witness is only able to arrive at the airport at 10.30 tomorrow, I am told by the court deputy she will not be here at the Tribunal before 12 noon, and then she has to be proofed by Mr. Ivetic. It does not appear to me that it is practicable to schedule a sitting for tomorrow in the circumstances, regrettably. Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is the afternoon not available? I haven't been able to check whether the afternoon the available or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, the afternoon is not available. We'll then have to sit on Monday as scheduled, and we would hear her first.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So in the circumstances, we are adjourned until --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise. One thing. I had forgotten to tender the last exhibit, ERN 0644-6670, the picture which I feel I ought to tender because the portion that was admitted into evidence by the Prosecution cuts off the patch that the gentleman testified about, so I'd ask for that to be tendered into evidence if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 1D 98, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you had something to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it can wait until Monday. I did want to address the Chamber on a legal point regarding this witness. If the Chamber wants to make some use of the time today, I'm happy to do it now. It would take 5 minutes, or I can do it prior to the witness's testimony on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you mean by a legal point because this is not the time for submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, no, but it has to do with my impeaching her with the statement of another. It was the issue that came up with MLD10 yesterday, and the same issue is arising with this witness. I failed to, I think, fully explain my position yesterday and wanted to see if I could do a better job of it today because it is an issue that arises with this particular witness, but I'm happy to do it Monday if the Chamber would prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let us hear you. Let us hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This has to do with the use of the other statement, when I think it's appropriate to use the statement of another witness and when it's not, and I think that perhaps the best way that I can explain this is just by taking kind of a rudimentary theoretical example. So let's say for some reason it became important to determine what colour sweater the witness wore yesterday, and statements were taken of you, Judge Robinson, and you state that it was a black sweater, and a statement was taken of you, Judge David, you described the sweater as being brown. Now, two distinctly factual situations arise during the taking of evidence about the colour of the sweater, and the factual difference has important implications for how a witness might be examined. The first situation would be when you, Judge Robinson, would be called to give evidence, consisting with your statement, you testified that the sweater is black. It would be improper to introduce on your cross-examination the statement of Judge David to establish that the sweater was not black but was brown. The Chamber I believe has correctly ruled that way in this trial, and that is the situation Mr. Ivetic referred to yesterday when he spoke about VG-64. In that case, the Defence sought to introduce the statement of her husband because it contradicted her. That is impermissible. If a party wants the benefit of Judge David's observations, that party should call Judge David as a witness. But there is another very different situation that can arise in a trial about the colour of the sweater. What if Judge Van Den Wyngaert were called to testify and her testimony was, I was not here yesterday, but Judge David told me that the witness wore a red sweater. It must be permissible to put Judge David's statement on the matter to Judge Van Den Wyngaert and ask whether or not she might be mistaken in her recollection of what Judge David said, mistaken because the person she is testifying as having said the sweater was red has in a sworn statement said the sweater was brown. With this next witness, she will be testifying to what her husband told her about the treatment -- his treatment of Zehra Turjacanin after the Bikavac fire. Dr. Vasiljevic, now deceased, gave sworn testimony before this Tribunal in 2001 where he described what happened when he treated Ms. Turjacanin. If she claims that her husband told her something different than his sworn account here, I must be able to put to her his testimony before the Tribunal and ask her whether or not she's mistaken. She's going to now sit in the very same seat her husband did when he testified about the very things she will give -- that he testified about, but she will give hearsay evidence about it. I believe the principles underlying the best evidence rule and the impeachment of witnesses both require that I be permitted to put the testimony of her husband, Dr. Vasiljevic, to her should she testify about something contradictory. I'd ask the Chamber to consider that, perhaps, over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, and Mr. Ivetic will also consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Consider -- do you require a submission, or -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you want to make a submission now on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I could do it -- I'd rather sit there and think about it for a while because I'm somewhat confused by it, especially given what I've read -- prior submissions in this case by Mr. Groome prior to my involvement in this case that seem opposite to what he's now proposing, but I'd like to have time to review that and make sure that my submissions are accurate and correctly spelled forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Consider it over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are adjourned until Monday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of January, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.
